gen-silkscreen-lora: Retro and lo-fi, Silkscreen spaces its pixel letters out like spaghetti laid flat. Lora, a classic serif, reads over a long stretch with gentle hairline thinning at the curves and a bookish, literary warmth.
gen-zen-dots-fs-gambetta: Gambetta reads gracefully, its serif strokes shifting in weight without ever turning dramatic. Zen Dots is best at friendly, tech-flavored display letters with generous room around each shape, and Gambetta is best at carrying bookish text.
gen-zen-dots-lora: Friendly tech, all room and roundness: Zen Dots keeps its openings generous at every weight, a clear contrast to the subtle pen-like modulation in Lora's bowls. Zen Dots grabs attention; Lora, a text serif, settles into literary reading.
gen-gf-unica-one-fs-alpino: Unica One draws every stroke at one thickness, with a huge lowercase eye. Alpino, a sans-serif, is the cozy, casual one, its tall body making the ascenders look short and its curve endings kept well apart.
gen-gf-autour-one-fs-merriweather-sans: Expressive Autour One keeps its g in one unchanging line weight, with clear channels leading into every round letter. And Merriweather Sans, a sans, would carry a long passage with sturdy, tall lowercase and an e that opens clearly to the right.
gen-gf-revalia-fs-nunito: Wide, bold and relaxed, Revalia strides across widely separated letters with an open-curved g. Nunito, a sans, answers by finishing its terminals well clear of the stem and rounding its lowercase bowls into something approachable.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-fs-quicksand: Tilt Neon's tube-like, constant-width stroke is what you notice first, topped off by a splayed c terminal. And Quicksand, a plain sans, softens the page with round, glass-bulb lowercase bowls and terminals that finish clear of the stem.
gen-gf-grandstander-fs-merriweather-sans: Chunky, open and cheerful, Grandstander holds its letters wide instead of curling them shut. And Merriweather Sans, a plain sans, brings tall, sturdy lowercase, so the strongest quality here is a big, confident readability.
gen-tourney-fs-nunito: Tourney cuts every stroke to one width and stretches its oversized small letters with wide tracking, giving an athletic punch. Nunito, a plain sans, then reads softly and smoothly with round bowls.
gen-syne-gf-esteban: Esteban, a serif with a refined, classic feel, has oversized lowercase and a wide-open e that never looks squeezed shut. Syne's bent-paperclip lines against that gentle swelling make the pair's strongest quality.
